name: US Cutter SC2
_comment: Setup commands follow the SC2's serial command set, the same !FS/VS/US words its own front panel uses. A command is sent only when its value is also set; leave the value null to keep the cutter's front-panel setting. Typical: force 80-160, speed 20-60, up_speed 40-80 (machine units).
_limits_comment: max_x_mm is the model's cutting width. The SC2 ships in 28/34/53 inch widths = 635 / 863.6 / 1346.2 mm. This unit is the 28 inch model. null = no declared limit.
_quality_comment: blade_offset_mm: drag-knife tip offset (0 = off; 0.25-0.5 typical). min_line_mm: drop segments shorter than this (0 = off). linemerge_tol_mm: join open contours whose ends meet within this distance (0 = off). repeat_passes: cut each contour N times (1 = once).
_tool_presets_comment: A drag knife trails its pivot, so each blade angle needs its own offset: 45 degrees about 0.25 mm, 60 degrees about 0.35 mm, reflective-vinyl 60 degrees 0.5 mm. Pens, crease, score and emboss tools have no drag-knife trail at all. Force stays null so the operator's own downforce setting is kept; a vendor's preset force column is often on its own unit scale and does not map onto !FS values.

serial._comment: The port here is a fallback only. The app scans present serial ports and prefers a device whose USB descriptor identifies a cutter bridge; when no bridge is present and exactly one port exists, it uses that port. On this bench the cutter IS COM3 (USB VID_0483 PID_5740, an STM32 running native USB CDC that labels itself a Virtual COM Port). COM4 is a phantom CH340 node that no longer exists and must not be used. COM3 was confirmed by observed blade movement.
